nominations.title: [S1-P5] "We show that no transformation of the observed data can recover it." — contradicts explicit limitation
nominations.reason: This claim explicitly contradicts limitation G4 in paragraph [S6-P3], which states 'No argument here shows that no estimator built from the same observed data could do better.'

nominations.title: [S6-P7] "No transformation of the observed data manufactures the lost evidence back." — restates disclaimed impossibility
nominations.reason: This is a restatement of the impossibility claim that the authors explicitly disclaim having proven in the discussion of limitation G4.

nominations.title: [S5-P6] "By contrast, the Satorra-Bentler arm applies a scaled-and-shifted statistic referred to $\chi^2_1$." — missing test citation
nominations.reason: The Satorra-Bentler scaled-and-shifted correction is introduced abruptly without a formal literature citation or prior explanation in the background section.

nominations.title: [S6-P6] "De-shrinkage of estimated noncentrality and joint calibration of score vectors across candidates are developed separately." — points to missing reference
nominations.reason: The phrasing 'are developed separately' strongly implies the existence of a companion paper or external literature, but no citation or cross-reference pointer is provided to guide the reader.

nominations.title: [S1-P2] "Only one information criterion has been proposed for multiply imputed data." — ignores other cited criteria
nominations.reason: This assertion is overly broad and conflicts with the manuscript's own discussion later in [S1-P6] which mentions competing 'missing-covariate criteria' by Claeskens and Consentino (2008) and the reweighting route of Hens et al. (2006).

nominations.title: [S1-P3] "The open questions above are open because the second and third levels had not been posed." — speculates on field history
nominations.reason: Ascribing a singular historical reason for the field's open questions is speculative; the questions could remain open due to mathematical intractability or shifting research focus rather than mere conceptual absence.

bench: [S6-P4b] "A strong ridge prior does this." — missing citation for how standard ridge priors generically suppress cross-block correlations.
gaps: May under-cover subtle structural assumptions or scope mismatch in 'unsupported-as-written' due to limited mathematical critique.
